open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove atomic completeness on the constrained shared-mechanism twin parameter space: for every regime and every query that is not \(m\)-separated in the replacement MAG, exhibit one admissible finite-alphabet shared-response-function parameter for which the corresponding selected pooled-law conditional-independence determinant is nonzero.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen kernels specify regime-local conditional laws but do not specify the cross-world coupling through the shared exogenous variables that determines conditioning on the basal event \(S^*=\mathbf 1\). Generic faithfulness for unrestricted discrete DAG conditional-probability tables does not apply to the resulting equality-constrained twin parameter space, and Dai et al. impose faithfulness rather than prove faithful realizability for every such replacement.
open_obligations.attempted: Extended the previous denominator-clearing argument to the full simultaneous problem. Once a finite-dimensional rational shared-response-function parameterization is supplied, simultaneous unfaithfulness is a finite union of algebraic exceptional sets. Shared basal coordinates create no further intersection problem. The remaining task is exactly to prove that, for each \(m\)-connected query, at least one determinant polynomial is nonzero on this constrained parameter space. Meek's unrestricted multinomial-DAG measure-zero theorem was checked and does not establish nontriviality after the twin equality constraints and fixed pooled weight are imposed.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Fix an admissible \(B\) and write \(\widetilde{\mathcal G}^{(k)}\) for the resulting regime-\(k\) twin DAG before marginalizing its latent vertices and conditioning on \(S^*=\mathbf 1\).  There is a precise algebraic reduction of the remaining problem.  Suppose one first supplies a finite-dimensional open parameter set \(\Theta\) for the shared response functions and exogenous distributions such that (i) the basal response functions are shared by all regimes at every non-target vertex, (ii) the indicator has probability \(1/2\) in each arm, (iii) \(\Pr_\theta(S^*=\mathbf 1)>0\), and (iv) every cell probability of every \(P_{\theta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) is a rational function of \(\theta\) whose denominator is positive on \(\Theta\).  For disjoint \(R_1,R_2,W\subseteq U_k\), conditional independence is then equivalent, cell by cell, to
\[
 p_\theta(r_1,r_2,w)p_\theta(w)
 -p_\theta(r_1,w)p_\theta(r_2,w)=0.
\]
Clearing the positive denominators gives finitely many polynomial equations \(q_{k,R_1,R_2,W,a}(\theta)=0\), where \(a\) ranges over the finitely many cell assignments.  The Markov direction supplied by the twin-DAG construction makes all these equations identities whenever \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are \(m\)-separated by \(W\) in \(M_k\).  For an \(m\)-connected query, it is enough to show that at least one corresponding polynomial is not the zero polynomial.  Indeed, choose one such nonzero polynomial for each of the finitely many regimes and \(m\)-connected queries, and multiply them.  Their product is nonzero because the real polynomial ring is an integral domain.  A nonzero real polynomial cannot vanish on a nonempty open set: this follows by induction on the number of coordinates, viewing it as a univariate polynomial on an open interval whose coefficient polynomials vanish on an open projection.  Hence the product cannot vanish throughout the nonempty open set \(\Theta\), and a point where it is nonzero makes all regime laws faithful simultaneously.  Notice that the shared basal coordinates cause no further finite-union difficulty: nontriviality may be certified separately for each query, although the final point is selected outside the union of all exceptional sets.

Strictly positive finite conditional tables can already be chosen on the replacement basal DAG, with the same table used in all regimes at every non-target vertex and with every selection table strictly positive.  This proves factorization, soft-intervention stability, and \(\Pr(S^*=\mathbf 1)>0\).  What is not supplied by the frozen core is the nontriviality certificate just isolated.  In particular, the recorded kernels \(\widetilde\kappa_v^{(j)}(dx_v\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})\) do not themselves specify the cross-world coupling between the reality variable, its basal copy, and their shared exogenous variable, although that coupling determines the law after conditioning on \(S^*=\mathbf 1\).  Meek's generic-faithfulness theorem for unrestricted multinomial Bayesian-network tables does not settle this restricted shared-response-function subspace.  Thus the exact residual claim is atomic completeness for every constrained replacement twin family: for each \(k\) and each \(m\)-connected query, construct one admissible shared-mechanism parameter at which the displayed determinant is nonzero.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a jointly faithful member of \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\); after such a member is available, all remaining conclusions follow from the proved graphical replacement lemma and the frozen definitions.
open_obligations.obstruction: The graphical replacement result fixes \(A\), every regime skeleton, and every unshielded collider, but membership in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) additionally requires the unresolved faithful selected pooled laws.
open_obligations.attempted: Completed the downstream implication equation by equation from a hypothetical jointly faithful realization. This shows that no separate compatibility-fiber or indicator-neighborhood argument remains; the sole missing premise is the atomic-completeness certificate isolated for \(\mathrm{lem:simultaneous\mbox{-}faithful\mbox{-}realization}\).
open_obligations.partial_result:
Assume only for this conditional derivation that the unresolved realization step supplies \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) whose pooled laws are faithful.  Membership in \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\), by \(\mathrm{def:replacement\mbox{-}realization\mbox{-}fiber}\), gives
\[
 \bigl(G_0(\widetilde\eta),(T_k(\widetilde\eta))_{k=1}^{K}\bigr)
 =\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B).
\]
The conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\) then yields
\[
 A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)
\]
and, for every \(k=0,\ldots,K\), equality of the skeleton and unshielded-collider signature of \(M_k(\widetilde\eta)\) and \(M_k(\eta)\) on the whole domain \(U_k\).  Because the proposed realization has positive selection probability, \(P_{\widetilde\eta}^{(0)}\) is defined.  Membership in \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) already includes membership in \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), and the realization lemma supplies its pooled-law faithfulness explicitly.  Therefore \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}signature}\) gives, component by component,
\[
 \mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)
 =\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_k(\widetilde\eta)),
          \operatorname{UC}(M_k(\widetilde\eta))\bigr)_{k=0}^{K}
 =\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O.
\]
It follows from \(\mathrm{def:compatibility\mbox{-}fiber}\) that \(\widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\).  Finally, the last conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\) gives, for each \(k\in[K]\),
\[
 Z_k=T_k(\widetilde\eta)
 \cup\bigl((F_k(\widetilde\eta)\setminus T_k(\widetilde\eta))
            \cap A(\widetilde\eta)\bigr).
\]
No step uses \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)=\kappa(\eta)\).  Hence every conclusion of the target follows formally from the graphical replacement lemma once the jointly faithful member exists; the only unproved implication is existence of that member.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Promote the empty-subgraph arrowhead specification and simple signature-monotone-path tail specification to jointly faithful whole-family models in \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The necessity directions and both opposing graphical constructions are complete, but the theorem quantifies over fully specified faithful models. The required promotion is precisely the unresolved simultaneous-realization lemma.
open_obligations.attempted: Completed the necessity proof using ancestor closure of \(A\) and descendant closure of every affected set, then verified all admissibility conditions for \(B=\varnothing\) and for a simple path in \(L_A\). The proved graphical replacement lemma preserves all oracle signatures. No endpoint-specific gap remains beyond faithful kernel realization.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(k\in[K]\), and an intervention-created adjacency \(uv\) with \(u,v\in A(\eta)\).  First consider any \(\eta'\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\), membership of \(u\) in \(Z_k\) is exactly affectedness of the ancestrally selected vertex \(u\), whether direct or indirect.  The same lemma's endpoint cases imply
\[
 \mu_{\eta'}(u)=\mathtt{arrow}
 \ \Longrightarrow\ u\in Z_k,
 \qquad
 \mu_{\eta'}(u)=\mathtt{tail}
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 \bigl(u\notin Z_k\bigr)
 \ \text{or}\ 
 u\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta')}(v).
\]
If the second alternative holds, take a directed basal path
\[
 u=x_0\to x_1\to\cdots\to x_m=v.
\]
The set \(A(\eta')=A(\eta)\) is ancestor closed: since \(v\) is an ancestor of a selection parent, every \(x_i\), being an ancestor of \(v\), is also an ancestor of a selection parent.  Thus every \(x_i\in A(\eta)\).  Each basal path edge is an edge of \(H[A(\eta)]\) by the observational-adjacency clause of \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\).  Moreover, for every \(\ell\in[K]\),
\[
 \ell\in\sigma(x_i)
 \ \Longrightarrow\ x_i\in Z_\ell
 \ \Longrightarrow\ x_i\in F_\ell(\eta')
 \ \Longrightarrow\ x_{i+1}\in F_\ell(\eta')
 \ \Longrightarrow\ x_{i+1}\in Z_\ell.
\]
The middle implication is descendant closure of \(F_\ell\), and the last uses \(x_{i+1}\in A(\eta')\) together with the indicator-neighbor formula in the same interface lemma.  Hence \(\sigma(x_i)\subseteq\sigma(x_{i+1})\) for every \(i\), so the path lies in \(L_{A(\eta)}\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\).  This proves both necessity directions.

The graphical converse is also complete.  If \(u\in Z_k\), choose \(B=\varnothing\).  In the replacement graph, \(u\) is affected and has no directed ancestry to the distinct selected vertex \(v\); the endpoint cases therefore put an arrowhead at \(u\).  If \(u\notin Z_k\), the endpoint cases put a tail at \(u\).  Finally, if \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\), choose a simple path from \(u\) to \(v\) in \(L_{A(\eta)}\) and let \(B\) contain exactly its directed edges.  This \(B\) is acyclic, lies in \(H[A(\eta)]\), respects signature inclusion, and creates no unshielded collider because no path vertex has two incoming \(B\)-edges.  The replacement makes \(u\) an ancestor of \(v\), and the endpoint cases put a tail at \(u\).  In all three cases \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\) preserves every full-domain regime signature and preserves \(A(\eta)\).  The retained-adjacency boundary is independently certified by \(\mathrm{prop:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}reduction}\).

Consequently the target theorem is proved at the graphical-specification level.  Promoting the empty graph and the simple-path graph to members of \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\) is exactly the unresolved jointly faithful realization assertion; no additional endpoint argument remains.
